title: FIDO2 Security Keys
description: Authenticates with FIDO2 security keys that sign challenges with device-bound private keys. The private key never leaves the token; each site gets a unique key pair. Phishing fails because the token checks the site's origin.
key_mechanisms: Register a key pair per site

demo.title: Demo — FIDO2 Security Keys

title: WebAuthn Integration
description: Integrates WebAuthn for passwordless login in browsers. The site requests credential creation or assertion; the browser mediates with the authenticator. It replaces passwords with public-key cryptography.

demo.title: Demo — WebAuthn Integration

title: CTAP2 Protocol
description: Speaks CTAP2 to authenticators over USB, NFC, or BLE. The client sends CBOR-encoded commands; the authenticator responds with signatures and attestations. It is the wire protocol under WebAuthn.

demo.title: Demo — CTAP2 Protocol

title: TPM-Backed Keys
description: Binds authentication keys to the TPM so they only work on the enrolled device. Keys are sealed to PCRs; a different machine cannot use them. Windows Hello uses this model.

demo.title: Demo — TPM-Backed Keys

title: Smart Card (PIV) Auth
description: Authenticates with PIV smart cards carrying certificates and private keys. The card signs challenges; PIN unlocks the card. Governments standardized on it for a reason.

demo.title: Demo — Smart Card (PIV) Auth

title: Attestation Verification
description: Verifies authenticator attestation to prove the key lives in genuine hardware. The attestation chain leads to the vendor's root; servers decide which models to trust. It closes the fake-token hole.

demo.title: Demo — Attestation Verification

title: PIN and User Verification
description: Requires PIN or biometrics on the token before it signs. User verification proves presence and consent; the token enforces retry limits. A stolen token without the PIN is useless.

demo.title: Demo — PIN and User Verification

title: Discoverable Credentials
description: Stores credentials on the authenticator so login needs no username first. The token lists its accounts for the site; the user picks one. Passkeys made this mainstream.

demo.title: Demo — Discoverable Credentials

title: Token Binding (TLS)
description: Binds tokens to the TLS channel so stolen tokens cannot be replayed elsewhere. The binding ID ties the token to the connection; a different channel invalidates it. It kills token theft.

demo.title: Demo — Token Binding (TLS)

title: HOTP/TOTP in Hardware
description: Generates one-time passwords in hardware tokens with protected seeds. The seed never leaves the device; codes change every 30 seconds. It is MFA's workhorse, phishing-prone but ubiquitous.

demo.title: Demo — HOTP/TOTP in Hardware

title: Secure Element APIs
description: Programs secure elements through standardized APIs for custom authentication. The SE isolates keys from the application processor; applets implement the protocol. It is hardware security for custom needs.

demo.title: Demo — Secure Element APIs

title: Enrollment Ceremonies
description: Enrolls tokens in supervised ceremonies binding identity to the credential. Identity proofing precedes key generation; the ceremony is witnessed and logged. It anchors trust at the start.

demo.title: Demo — Enrollment Ceremonies

title: Recovery Codes
description: Issues single-use recovery codes for lost-token scenarios. Codes are generated cryptographically and stored hashed; each works once. It is the safety net that must itself be protected.

demo.title: Demo — Recovery Codes

title: Phishing-Resistant Deployment
description: Deploys only phishing-resistant factors: FIDO2 and smart cards, not SMS or TOTP. Policy enforces the strong factors; weaker ones are disabled. It is the single highest-ROI security upgrade.

demo.title: Demo — Phishing-Resistant Deployment

title: Enterprise Token Revocation
description: Revokes tokens instantly on loss or departure across all systems. Central revocation lists propagate to every verifier; sessions tied to the token die. Speed matters more than ceremony here.

demo.title: Demo — Enterprise Token Revocation
